Sports.title: Erling Haaland pulled away from furious clash on physical night that included tunnel fight and goal records
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland pulled away from furious clash on physical night that included tunnel fight and goal records

Erling Haaland had to be dragged away from a heated incident during Manchester City's Champions League win over Porto.

Tensions boiled over in second-half stoppage time as Man City began their European campaign with a 2-0 win in Portugal thanks to a brace from Haaland.



4 Against Porto, Haaland scored his 59th Champions League goal, in 59 games - Lionel Messi needed 80 games to score 60 Credit: Getty

And the striker was at the centre of the flash point, clashing with Porto's Pablo Rosario and sparking a melee on the pitch.

Haaland was hurled to the ground by Rosario, with both players booked by referee Szymon Marciniak.

But talkSPORT's Adrian Durham wasn't impressed with the Porto man at all and took issue with Marciniak's officiating of the incident.



"Really naive refereeing," Durham said on air. "Rosario's basically trying to get Haaland sent off and it's a disgrace. Really poor refereeing, that."

It wasn't the first coming together of its nature on the night at the Estadio do Dragao.



Security staff had to step in as players and officials from both sides clashed at half time.

Porto had taken issue when Gabri Veiga was left bleeding from his head after being accidentally struck by Marc Guehi's trailing arm during an aerial challenge.



Guehi escaped any punishment – much to Porto's dismay – on a night which, perhaps surprisingly given how things flared up, saw only three players booked: Rosario, Haaland and his City teammate Josko Gvardiol.

What did Enzo Maresca say?

“It was the complete performance on the ball and off the ball for 95 minutes,” the City boss said.

“We created enough chances to win the game in the first half and their goalkeeper was very good.

4 A challenge that floored Veiga sparked angry scenes at half-time in a tunnel bust-up between the sides Credit: Getty



4 Haaland was pulled away from a scuffle with Rosario and the pair were booked at the end of the game Credit: Getty

“We tried to continue in the second half in the same way.

“It’s game by game. It’s a different competition, different stadium but the most important thing is we show who we are.

“We try to be aggressive off the ball and on the ball try to plan how we can win the game.

“In terms of where we are, I don’t know. I can see game after game, the team is improving.”



Maresca added he was happy with the way his side coped with the physical nature of the contest.

“We know in these games, when you come here it’s difficult.

“That’s the way they grow up but it’s normal. We dealt with it very good.

“I watch games from the Portuguese league, especially now with Porto and Sporting. I watch different games and you can see the level is very high.

“Porto play very good, [Porto manager Francesco Farioli] is doing a fantastic job but we managed it and won the game.”



What milestone did Haaland achieve?

That late scuffle aside, it was a celebratory, historic occasion for Haaland.

In scoring his fourth and fifth goals of the season, and his 166th and 167th overall for City, he moved up to third on the club's all-time leading scorers list.

It represents a remarkable achievement for Haaland, who only moved to the Etihad Stadium four years ago but will be going for his fourth Premier League Golden Boot in five seasons in 2026/27.

Since arriving from Borussia Dortmund in 2022, he's gone along at a truly prolific average of 0.82 goals per game in all competitions.



4 Against Porto, Haaland equalled Aguero's 36 Champions League goals for Man City

The 26-year-old now has only Eric Brook (177 goals) and Sergio Aguero (still well out in front on 260 goals) left to catch.

That being said, Haaland has already emulated Aguero in one respect, drawing level with him for the most Champions League goals for City with 36.

Haaland also goes clear of Bayern Munich legend Thomas Muller to take seventh place outright on the all-time list of leading Champions League scorers with 59 in total – at a remarkable average of exactly one a game.



For some comparison, it took Lionel Messi 80 Champions League appearances to reach 60 goals in the competition.

The Champions League continues

Elsewhere on the opening night of Champions League action, Aston Villa got their first win of the season, edging a 3-2 thriller against Club Brugge.

Two more English clubs are in action on Wednesday: Liverpool entertain Atletico Madrid and Arsenal travel to Napoli, amid travel chaos due to air traffic control issues in the UK.

Arsenal's game is live on talkSPORT 2, with Manchester United's home Champions League opener against Sabah on Thursday live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Scott McTominay undergoes heart surgery as Napoli give return timeline
Sports.content:
Scott McTominay has undergone successful surgery on a heart issue, Napoli have confirmed.

McTominay was diagnosed with mild benign arrhythmia, which is an irregular heartbeat.



2 McTominay has had surgery on a heart issue Credit: AFP

A statement from Napoli read: "On Tuesday morning, Scott McTominay underwent an ablation procedure at Spire Manchester Hospital. The operation was a complete success.

McTominay will rest for two weeks and then resume training."

What is cardiac arrhythmia ablation?

Cardiac arrhythmia ablation is a short procedure that, according to the British Heart Foundation, can last as little as just 15 minutes.

During surgery, a small cut is made on the patient's groin or wrist, with catheters are then placed inside and moved up to the heart.



The area inside the heart that has caused the arrhythmia is then destroyed by either radiofrequency energy or cryoablation.

This step of the procedure helps to block abnormal electrical signals in the heart.



McTominay played in Napoli's first two Serie A fixtures this season and was brought off in the 2-1 defeat to Como.

Max Allegri's side are back in action at home to Arsenal in their Champions League opener on Wednesday, live on talkSPORT 2.



Napoli previously expected McTominay to be out of action until mid-October.

If that is still the case, he would miss Scotland's upcoming internationals. Scotland have four fixtures scheduled for the newly extended international break beginning later this month.

2 McTominay could miss the international break with Scotland Credit: Getty

Slovenia, Switzerland and North Macedonia are their Nations League opponents as they begin their Group B1 campaign.



Sebastien Pocognoli will take charge of the side for the first time since being announced as the replacement for Steve Clarke.

The former Belgium and Premier League defender was previously with the Belgian U18s, Royale Union Saint-Gilloise and AS Monaco.

Pocognoli has joined a Scotland team that had a miserable World Cup campaign during the summer.

They scored one goal across their three group matches and missed out on the knockout stages.



McTominay played every minute as Scotland returned to the tournament for the first time since 1998.

Sports.title: Borussia Dortmund player rushed to hospital after being stretchered off pitch in worrying scenes
Sports.content:
Borussia Dortmund player rushed to hospital after being stretchered off pitch in worrying scenes

Borussia Dortmund winger Konstantinos Karetsas was rushed to hospital shortly after being stretched off against Villarreal.

The 18-year-old worryingly sat down on the pitch unchallenged in the 23rd minute of the Champions League match.



4 Karetsas dropped to the turf in worrying scenes on Tuesday Credit: Getty

4 Medics carried the teenager from the pitch before taking him to hospital Credit: AFP

Dortmund confirmed that the Greece international had been taken to hospital after suffering ‘circulation problems’.

Fans in attendance at Signal Iduna Park were understandably concerned by the player’s bad turn.



The club were quick to inform supporters of Karetsas’ condition and whereabouts.

They wrote on X: “Konstantinos Karetsas had to leave the pitch in the game against Villarreal due to circulation problems.



“Kosta is doing as well as can be expected given the circumstances, and he is on his way to the hospital for further examinations.”

He was quickly replaced by Arsenal star Ethan Nwaneri who joined the Bundesliga side on a season-long loan.



Borussia Dortmund 3-2 Villarreal

Dortmund had already suffered a huge injury blow with fellow summer signing Giannis Konstantelias suffered an Anterior Cruciate Ligament injury on the opening weekend of the season.

The injury is likely to keep him out of action for much of the campaign.

Nico Kovac's side were quick to regroup after the interval and showed their quality in an action-packed second half which saw Dortmund edge a five-goal thriller.

They were given a helping hand in eight minutes after half time thanks to an own goal from former Chelsea defender Renato Veiga.



4 Karetsas was a summer signing from Belgian club Genk Credit: Getty

Santiago Mourino leveled shortly afterwards for the La Liga side until Dortmund striker Sehrou Guirassy took centre stage.

The Guinean netted twice in the final ten minutes to hand his side a crucial three points.

He then incredibly put through his own net in the third minute of added time to put a nervous spin on the final exchanges.



Dortmund are not among the favourites to lift the Champions League but boast plenty of know how in reaching the latter stages,

Winners of the competition in 1997, Dortmund have since contested two finals - both stages at Wembley.

They were beaten 2-1 by Bayern Munich in an all-German affair in 2013.

4 Serhou Guirassy was decisive against Villarreal - at both ends! Credit: Getty



Their second attempt at glory came in 2024 but slipped to a 2-0 defeat to a Vinicius Junior-inspired Real Madrid.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi reportedly agrees deal to buy 100 per cent stake in second tier club
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi reportedly agrees deal to buy 100 per cent stake in second tier club

Lionel Messi has reportedly agreed a deal in principle to buy Spanish second tier club Eldense.

Diario AS reports that the eight-time Ballon d'Or-winning superstar has reached an agreement to acquire 100 per cent of Eldense's shares.



2 Messi has retired from Argentina duty but is still playing for Inter Miami Credit: Getty

The report adds that Messi's lawyers had been in talks for some time with the club's current owners, the Colombian investment group TH – led by Juan Carlos Trujillo.

Eldense have just returned to LaLiga2, the second tier of Spanish football, winning promotion back to the division at the first time of asking having been relegated in the 2024/25 season.

Based in the Valencian city of Elda, Eldense are managed by former Spain striker Claudio Barragan, who won six caps for La Roja in the early 90s.



Founded in 1921, they play their home games at the 5,776-capacity Estadio Municipal Nuevo Pepico Amat.

Messi's involvement already goes beyond the pitch

This wouldn't be Messi's first venture into club ownership.

The 39-year-old Argentine – who recently announced his retirement from international football following an epic career in which he captained his country to World Cup glory – took full ownership of third-tier outfit Cornella back in April.



But Eldense would be the first professional club in his portfolio.

Messi's prospective investment is said to be a solo endeavour without the support of any partners.

The greatest of all time?

It was in Spain where Messi ascended to all-time great status, during 17 glittering years with Barcelona.



A ten-time LaLiga champion and four-time Champions League winner with Barca, Messi played 778 games to top the club's all time appearances list – not to mention amassing 672 goals to obliterate their all-time scoring record.

2 Messi averaged 0.86 goals per game for Barcelona Credit: Getty

He won six of his eight Ballons d'Or as a Barca player, before leaving in 2021 an undisputed icon.

After a two-year stint with Paris Saint-Germain, he headed to MLS to join Inter Miami in 2023.



Messi in good company among current pros

Messi isn't the only active player to have dipped their toes into the world of club ownership and he joins, among others, his great contemporary Cristiano Ronaldo.

Ronaldo purchased a 25 per cent stake in another LaLiga2 outfit, Almeria, in February this year.

Last year, Croatia legend Luka Modric became a minority investor in Championship Swansea City.

In 2024, Kylian Mbappe's Coalition Capital investment fund bought an 80 per cent stake in French club Caen.



And the previous year, fellow France star N'Golo Kante struck a deal to take over as owner of Belgian outfit Royal Excelsior Vitron.

Sports.title: Hilarious moment Micah Richards runs out of the CBS studio when Kylian Mbappe names him his favourite pundit - after he wrote him a poem and they shared bizarre virtual hug
Sports.content:
Micah Richards struggled to contain his excitement and ran out of the CBS Sports studio after being named Kylian Mbappe's favourite pundit on Tuesday night.

Mbappe joined US network CBS for a post-match interview after scoring in Real Madrid's 2-1 victory over Inter Milan in the Champions League, and Richards was so excited to speak to the striker that he even wrote him a poem.

As host Kate Abdo revealed Mbappe was joining the show for the first time in six years, Richards cheered in excitement and bellowed: 'Kylian! Finally we meet my friend.'

Overjoyed, the ex-England international danced over to the big screen to give a hug to Mbappe, who laughed and joined him in the bizarre virtual embrace, before returning to his seat to read a short poem to the Frenchman.

'Speed like lightning, a finish so clean,' he began. 'Kylian Mbappe, the football machine.

'From Paris to Madrid, he's chasing his dream. A star of the pitch, the king of the scene. My man!'

Who's @KMbappe's favorite on the #UCLToday show?



Not sure @micahrichards is ever going to recover from this 😂 pic.twitter.com/bnFBwuXAp9 — CBS Sports Golazo ⚽️ (@CBSSportsGolazo) September 8, 2026

Micah Richards ran out the CBS studio after Kylian Mbappe called him his favourite pundit

The former Man City defender was overjoyed after Mbappe joined the network for an interview

After buttering up the striker, Richards asked at the end of the interview: 'Who's your favourite on the show, baby?'

To the pundit's delight, Mbappe replied: 'I would have to say you.'

Richards immediately jumped to his feet in celebration and pulled out Alan Shearer's iconic celebration, raising his arm aloft as he charged out of the studio saying: 'See you later, I'm retiring now!'

His reaction has since gone viral, with more than 10,000 fans liking CBS Sports' clip of the moment after it was posted to social media platform X on Tuesday night.

During the interview, Mbappe spoke highly of his new Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho, praising the legendary manager after his side made a positive start in the Champions League.

'Jose Mourinho makes you feel alive,' the Ballon d'Or nominee said. 'He makes you feel special. He is a guy who puts a lot of pressure and high intensity in training.

'He talks a lot with the players, and we know what he wants from us, what he expects from us.

The France international saw the funny side after Richards wrote him a flattering poem

It's been six years in the making for @MicahRichards 🫂@KMbappe gets the warmest of welcomes on UCL Today 😂 pic.twitter.com/ht8YcJn6r6 — CBS Sports Golazo ⚽️ (@CBSSportsGolazo) September 8, 2026

Just when you think you’ve seen it all… @MicahRichards has written a poem for @KMbappe ✍️😭 pic.twitter.com/g4VPZoB9rt — CBS Sports Golazo ⚽️ (@CBSSportsGolazo) September 8, 2026

'When a coach gives you that confidence and that hunger, you do not want to disappoint him, and you want to give your best.'

After the match, which saw Mbappe and Federico Valverde strike for Los Blancos in the 2-1 win, Mourinho returned the compliment to his superstar forward.

'I rank him right up there among the players I've coached,' Mourinho admitted.

'I don't like comparisons... I've had players like Ronaldo Nazario. But Kylian is right up there! Kylian is incredible.'

Sports.title: Carlos Alcaraz's vomit-stained 3.33am nightmare in New York! Defending champion throws up into a towel as he's knocked out of US Open by Ben Shelton in latest ever finish to a match
Sports.content:
Carlos Alcaraz's vomit-stained 3.33am nightmare in New York! Defending champion throws up into a towel as he's knocked out of US Open by Ben Shelton in latest ever finish to a match

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Behind the baseline inside Arthur Ashe Stadium, the clocks ticked beyond 2:50am. It was Wednesday morning. A school day. Sunrise was only a few hours away. And yet? With the help of several thousand New Yorkers - some drunk, some asleep, the rest simply delirious - Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton dragged the US Open into uncharted waters.

Never in history had a match here finished this late. Never before had these two put on such a spectacle. But after four and a half sets and nearly four hours, the curtain refused to fall on this quarterfinal.

It was exhausting. It was intoxicating. And for Alcaraz, it was sickening. Before the start of the deciding set, the defending champion appeared to vomit into his towel. But still it went on. All the way until road's end: a fifth-set tiebreak.

All the way until 3:33am, when after four hours and 28 minutes, Ben Shelton fired down an 146mph ace, stuck out his tongue, pulled Alcaraz into a long embrace and then - at long, long last - soaked up the biggest moment of his young career.

The scoreline - 6-7 6-1 6-3 1-6 7-6 - spoke to the undulating chaos of the occasion: as night gave way to morning, this match swung back and forth between two of the most electrifying talents in tennis. In the end, it was Shelton and his hammer serve that won out.

What a player. What a night. What a shame someone had to lose. And what a travesty most of the world slept through it. Forget, for a moment, the incredible theater on this long night in New York. What are we doing? Who wins from starting a game after 11pm - beyond a few insomniacs, TV viewers on the other side of the world, and Shelton's semifinal opponent Frances Tiafoe?

Carlos Alcaraz was seen throwing up into a towel as he was knocked out of the US Open

Alcaraz was clearly struggling during the match - which ended in defeat at 3.30am local time

An ecstatic Ben Shelton celebrates beating Alcaraz in the latest ever finish at the US Open

'I am just hoping that my best friend and my sister over there don’t have to be at work at 6am – in three hours,' Shelton said. 'It would be huge for their employers to let them have the day off today.'

The American added: 'I am so grateful, so blessed. God has blessed in so many ways... sharing the court with Carlos is an absolute honor and I cherish every moment I have out here.'

Alcaraz has now played in the two latest finishes in US Open history. Back in 2022, en route to his first title in New York, the Spaniard beat Jannik Sinner at 2:50am. How we missed him over those four months when his wrist betrayed him.

With this defeat, Alcaraz's title defense is over. With this win, Shelton ended a run of 17 matches without victory over a top-three player. He has ensured an American will be in the final and a new name will be on the trophy.

It was at 11:05pm local time – after more than 13 hours of action and a final plea to influencers not to use Arthur Ashe Stadium for a personal photoshoot - Shelton and Alcaraz were finally ready to bring the curtain down on Day 11.

They had just over three and half hours to wrap this up or risk breaking new ground. They failed. Of course they failed. This showdown with Shelton had all the ingredients to be a blockbuster, another marathon tug of war.

But the 23,000 fans who forked out for this night session – including Seal, Simone Biles and Kevin Hart – knew the risk they ran. Unlike at Wimbledon, there is no 11pm curfew here. Only last week, Venus Williams’ first-round match kicked off at 12:13am – a US Open record – and on his way to the quarterfinals, No 1 seed Alexander Zverev has already clocked off at 1:55am and 2:15am.

Shelton had played beyond 2am in the second round and there was nothing sleepy about the way he began this match.

For 12 games and most of a breathless first-set tiebreak, the American went toe-to-toe with Alcaraz. Time and again, this contest delivered on its promise of swagger and vicious shot-making.

And yet it felt so predictable, so ominous, when – at 5-5 – Shelton was broken to love. How often do we see the very best find a way just when a set teeters on a knife edge? This time, though, Shelton did not yield. At least not immediately. He broke back before taking control of the tiebreak.

Shelton's girlfriend Trinity Rodman stayed until the bitter end as her partner beat Alcaraz

But some members of the crowd were less engaged with the late finish in the quarter-final

One astonishing rally, in which the American pulled Alcaraz from back to a front like a yo-yo, sent Arthur Ashe into a frenzy. Only one member of the crowd was not lost in rapture: Shelton’s father, Bryan, who gestured for his son to calm down.

The 23-year-old heeded his advice and looked set to steal the set when he led 5-3 in the tiebreak. But then, Alcaraz found something from somewhere. Four points later, he had drawn first blood.

That was the trigger for many inside Arthur Ashe to call it a night. Who could blame them for thinking the dye was cast? Thankfully Shelton didn’t see it that way – even after squandering four break points in the opening game of the second set.

The American’s pressure finally told two games later and, this time, Alcaraz had no immediate answer. So Shelton turned the screw, breaking three times in succession to take the set 6-1. It was 12:56am, we had a game on our hands and the stadium speakers blasted out Jay Z’s reminder that this ‘city never sleeps.’

You’d do well to doze off in earshot of ‘DJ Mode’ at the best of times. Let alone with this quarterfinal so finely poised.

And yet, by the time Alcaraz and Shelton climbed out of their chairs, more and more fans were on their way home. At this point, nowhere was more sparsely filled than courtside where a single seat can cost up to $5,000.

Those who remained in the posh seats were treated to more majesty at either end of the third set: first, a remarkable rally that saw Shelton stretch and contort every fiber of his 6ft 4in frame.

After 18 shots, Alcaraz eventually claimed the point before cupping his hand behind his ear. And then, half an hour later, the Spaniard won a battle of touch around the net. Even Shelton’s girlfriend – soccer star Trinity Rodman – rose to her feet to applaud.

With this win, Shelton ended a run of 17 matches without victory over a top-three player

Alcaraz recovered from two sets to one down to force a decider, only to lose on a tiebreak

Unfortunately for Alcaraz, neither made a difference as Shelton held firm to take the third set. This time, his father was his biggest hype man. At the other end, Alcaraz bent at the waist. It was 1:43am and those four-and-half months off appeared to be catching up with the No 2 seed. He was grimacing and chuntering and soon Alcaraz faced more break points.

This time, though, he saved them and then, out of nowhere, he put dent after dent in Shelton’s serve. Alcaraz won five of the next six games to send this to a decider. It was 2:20am and we were headed toward more history on Arthur Ashe.

How much had that taken out of the defending champion? As thousands of fans – many of whom had migrated from the nosebleeds to the lower bowl – bayed for more, Alcaraz appeared to vomit into his towel.

And yet, as this match ticked towards a fifth hour, the Spaniard seemed to find a second - third? fourth? - wind. He opened up a break-point opportunity and repelled Shelton as the American banged at the door. By the time Alcaraz sent this to a tiebreak, it was 3:21am. At long, long last. Something had to give. In the end, it was Alcaraz who broke and Shelton who marched into a second US Open semifinal. After this, who would bet on him stopping there?

Sports.title: The three things Arsenal need to do this season to finally win the Champions League - from the players Mikel Arteta must learn to trust to the January transfer window plan and a returning hero
Sports.content:
The three things Arsenal need to do this season to finally win the Champions League - from the players Mikel Arteta must learn to trust to the January transfer window plan and a returning hero

The Hilton Budapest had been primed, a function room already booked in advance for Arsenal’s staff and players after last season’s Champions League final.

But instead of a raucous party to mark a first European Cup in the club’s 140-year history, a few reflective, sorrows-drowning drinks followed before an early flight back to London for the Premier League title parade through the streets of north London.

The disappointment exuding from Mikel Arteta in the post-match press conference following the defeat on penalties by Paris Saint-Germain was marked. Ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title had gone out the window, his words verged on anger.

‘Pain, that's it, when you are so close in the competition and you are a few penalty kicks away from winning the biggest football club competition, that's the way which you feel,’ he said.

After ending that long, agonising wait to be crowned champions of England, conquering Europe is Arteta's final frontier. The Spaniard has never tasted success in a European competition as a player or manager, and often uses the Champions League as a reference point in how legacies are defined.

Arsenal are well primed to make that final step. They were, after all, only a few kicks from glory in May, and have strengthened further this summer with additions such as Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa. But how do they get over that final hurdle?

Mikel Arteta's side were a penalty shootout away from finally lifting their first European Cup against Paris Saint-Germain in Budapest in May

Gabriel's decisive miss from the spot was an agonising end to a season that could have been historic

1. Trust the depth

Arsenal’s squad depth gives Arteta the luxury of rotating without necessarily weakening the starting XI.

Ben White has made a case to continue at right back even when Jurrien Timber returns from injury, his telepathic connection with Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard forming a triumvirate which opponents have difficulty stopping on the right flank.

In the middle, Myles Lewis-Skelly has performed well in place of the injured Bruno Guimaraes. The new £75million Brazilian is expected to walk into the line-up on Wednesday against Napoli but after his recent displays, Lewis-Skelly will be on the Brazilian’s heels if there’s any dip in form. It’s a great situation to have for Arteta. But he still needs to utilise it.

Last season, he arguably gave far too many minutes to Declan Rice when he was already tiring, for example. The England midfielder, who went on to play a key role at the World Cup, made 55 appearances in all competitions, with 49 starts and 4,454 minutes, or 91 per cent of Arsenal's minutes when he was available for selection. No Arsenal outfielder played more. Rice himself during the World Cup admitted he had been playing through neural pain in his hamstring since December.

Arsenal had four outfield players above 4,200 minutes - Rice, Martin Zubimendi (4,298), William Saliba (4,254) and Gabriel (4,210). This level of excessive workload must be better shared if Arsenal are to go all the way to the final again, and potentially lift the elusive trophy.

Zubimendi and Rice's back-up, Christian Norgaard, were not trusted to give the Spaniard a rest, but now Lewis-Skelly or Guimaraes can offer that. Konsa can cover while Saliba and Cristhian Mosquera are injured, and Piero Hincapie can slot seamlessly in if Gabriel needs a spell out.

Even Arteta hinted at this in Budapest after the defeat by PSG, saying: ‘You have to get into the competition with all the squad available in the best moment, each player. And we've had more players, many more players than last season but not all of them in that condition for different reasons. And that's something we have to improve as well.’ At least he’s aware. Now he needs to trust those on the bench to get him through.

Declan Rice has spoken of the neural pain he suffered from this summer, and surely cannot keep on playing as many minutes as he did last season

In Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes, Arteta has two high-class options he can call on to give Rice a rest

2. Go again in January

Viktor Gyokeres has fallen down the pecking order with Kai Havertz fully fit.

It was always the plan last season, but an injury to Havertz on the opening day at Old Trafford last season resulted in Gyokeres becoming the Gunners’ first-choice striker in the previous campaign, where he struck 21 goals across all competitions after joining for £56million.

The Swede, though, has only made one substitute appearance in three league matches, coming off the bench for 12 minutes against Chelsea on Sunday and showing signs of rust.

After Havertz and Gyokeres, though, Arteta’s options thin out dramatically. Midfielder Mikel Merino could once again be thrown up front to fill the gap, though this would not be ideal. Having failed in their chase for either Vinicius Junior, Julian Alvarez or Lautaro Martinez, Arsenal are very light in the striker position.

It begs the question: can the club lure the likes of Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi in the January window? He’s a player Arteta admires, has a special place in fans' hearts after scoring the goal that helped seal the title in May and could provide the firepower needed to get Arsenal over the line in Europe too.

Eli Junior Kroupi scored home and away for Bournemouth against Arsenal last season - could he be the missing piece in Arteta's puzzle?

3. Timber's limbering up

The importance of Timber can’t be overstated. In the Budapest defeat, the Dutchman was only half-fit, and came on for an out-of-place Mosquera only after the Spaniard had given away a penalty for a lunge on PSG's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Timber is defensively solid, rarely bypassed by opposition players and commits forward with overlaps, too, in the final third. When fully firing, he is arguably the best right back in the league, and was voted as such in the PFA Team of the Year last season.

The 25-year-old trained on Tuesday morning and is in the squad for Wednesday’s fixture against Napoli.

Timber’s return has been a long, arduous journey from a groin injury which had affected him since March. It ruled him out of the Netherlands’ World Cup squad before returning to light training sessions at the start of Arsenal’s pre-season in July.

If the Gunners can have Timber fully fit for the latter stages of the competition, that is a huge plus.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher pokes fun at how he faces being declared BANKRUPT over '£800,000 tax bill' - after TV host Kate Abdo mocked 'depleted bank account'
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher was the target of a string of bankruptcy jokes during CBS Sports’ first Champions League show of the season on Tuesday, less than a week after HMRC took action over the Liverpool legend’s substantial unpaid tax bill.

HMRC filed a petition at the High Court in London last Wednesday to have the Sky Sports pundit and former England footballer declared bankrupt over an unpaid tax bill which is reported to be in the region of £700,000 to £800,000.

CBS Sports, whose Champions League coverage is renowned for putting humour front and centre, wasted no time poking fun at Carragher over the matter on Tuesday.

Host Kate Abdo, who was joined by Carragher, Micah Richards and Thierry Henry in the CBS Sports studio, said: 'A busy hot summer can be taxing. Not for this man, Liverpool legend Jamie Carragher. A man whose career stats are more depleted than Jamie's bank account.'

Carragher and Richards reacted with roars of laughter in the studio, clearly seeing the funny side.

Interjecting midway through Abdo's joke, the former Liverpool centre-back suggested the HMRC bankruptcy petition is resolved, as he said: 'All paid, all done.'

Jamie Carragher poked fun at how he faces being declared bankrupt over a '£800,000 tax bill'

Later in the show, when previewing Barcelona's clash against Feyenoord on Wednesday night, Carragher also took the opportunity to mock himself over the matter.

'They (Barcelona) have probably had financial problems, haven't they. Well, haven't we all,' the former England international joked to the amusement of his peers.

Last week, a spokesperson for HMRC told Daily Mail Sport: 'We take a supportive approach to dealing with customers who have tax debts and do everything we can to help those who engage with us to get out of debt, such as offering instalment plans. We only petition for bankruptcy as a last resort.'

HMRC added that it does not comment on individual cases.

Carragher, 48, is listed as a director at four firms and as a LLP Member for another. As well as covering the Champions League with the US network, he is a regular pundit on Sky Sports and appears routinely on the Stick To Football podcast, run by Gary Neville's media business The Overlap.

A spokesperson for Carragher told Daily Mail Sport: 'This is a private tax matter that should have been resolved sooner, and the appropriate steps are being taken today to settle it.

'It is understood that the matter will not proceed any further and will be resolved imminently.'

The BBC reported that the bill is around £700,000 to £800,000.

CBS Sports host Kate Abdo mocked the Liverpool legend over his 'depleted bank account'

Carragher has been married to his wife Nicola for 21 years - pictured at Royal Ascot in June

Carragher is the founder of the 23 Foundation, an organisation aiming to help young people in Merseyside, and is a co-founder of Football For Change, which helps to tackle child poverty through education, sport and training.

He is married to his wife of 21 years, Nicola, and together they have two children: James, 23, who plays as a defender for League One club Wigan Athletic, and actress and model Mia, 22.

Sports.title: Jessica Pegula overcomes Emma Navarro in battle of the US Open billionaires to set up semifinal showdown with Aryna Sabalenka
Sports.content:
Both Jessica Pegula and Emma Navarro have long been adamant about one thing: no one gave them any handouts. They may be the daughters of billionaires and the heiresses to business empires worth a combined $15billion. But no leg of their long road to Arthur Ashe Stadium was easy. Or bought.

There were times in this all-American clash, however, when both Pegula and Navarro seemed intent on offering their opponent a shortcut toward the US Open semifinals.

Between them, they hit 10 double faults in a tense, trying opening set that Navarro took 6-3. Time and again they broke serve and then immediately ceded that advantage.

But Pegula has made a habit of reviving herself from slow starts and the No 3 seed levelled this match after Navarro – with the second set on a knife edge - hit another costly double fault.

No prizes for guessing what happened in the decider. More crucial double faults. More missed opportunities. More back-to-back breaks of serve.

Until eventually, after nearly two hours, Pegula completed her comeback to reach the last four with a 3-6 6-4 6-3 win.

Jessica Pegula overcame Emma Navarro to set up a semifinal showdown with Aryna Sabalenka

Navarro, the No 26 seed, took the first set 6-3 but was unable to hold on to her advantage

After she secured the three-set victory, Pegula roared with relief inside Arthur Ashe Stadium

It had precious little of the drama that Frances Tiafoe and Alex Michelsen delivered a few hours earlier. Frankly, it wasn’t a great watch at all. And that felt particularly cruel on this Arthur Ashe crowd – their evening session started more than an hour late and every twist in this quarterfinal meant a longer wait for Ben Shelton’s blockbuster clash with Carlos Alcaraz.

By the end, there were long, tired faces in the stands and even ironic cheers as the end of this quarterfinal edged closer.

Not that Pegula will care one jot. She can play far better than this and she will need to with Aryna Sabalenka standing between the No 3 seed and a second US Open final.

With this win, she has at least sealed $1.45million in prize money. Not that it would have made much difference to either family’s coffers.

Navarro's father, Ben, made a fortune in credit cards and debt collection. His net worth is estimated to be $3.2billion.

As for Pegula? Her dad, Terry, grew rich through oil and gas and - together with his wife, Kim - now owns the NHL's Buffalo Sabres and the NFL's Buffalo Bills. The Pegulas are thought to be worth nearly $12billion.

By the time the family amassed its fortune, however, Pegula was already a teenager and on her way toward the top of tennis.

She has risen to become the highest-ranked American woman in the world. But still a major title eludes her.

Pegula, left, with her family after her parents Terry and Kim bought the Buffalo Bills in 2014

Ben Navarro began his career on Wall Street and is estimated by Forbes to be worth $3.2billion

Join the discussion Does family wealth in sports give some athletes unfair advantages, or does talent always win out?

Navarro, meanwhile, will rue this loss and this missed opportunity to reach a second US Open semifinal. But the 25-year-old, who was forced to take two months off earlier this year after struggles with her health, can still reflect on a fine end to 2026. She will be back.

On Tuesday night, it took almost half an hour for Pegula and Navarro to finish the opening five games as these American rivals traded double faults and breaks of serve. Pegula missed five second serves in her opening three service games and it didn’t take long for the No 3 seed’s emotions to boil over.

Navarro left the door ajar with wobbles of her own – she, too, made five double faults in the opening set - but after Pegula converted just one of five break-point opportunities, the underdog took the first set 6-3.

From there, thankfully, the double faults subsided for a while. Instead these two tussled their way to 4-4 in the second set. Pegula held serve, Navarro stumbled – at 4-5, 30-30, the No 26 seed hit her sixth double fault of the match. That was all Pegula needed to tie things up.

Forty-five minutes later, when she finally won this arm wrestle, Pegula clenched her fist and let out a roar of relief. She wasn’t the only one who was glad this was over.

Sports.title: How Cody Gakpo became Liverpool's flying Dutchman again: Daily meetings with Andoni Iraola, why his Man City move collapsed, his exemplary personality behind the scenes - and the key to unlocking his best form
Sports.content:
How Cody Gakpo became Liverpool's flying Dutchman again: Daily meetings with Andoni Iraola, why his Man City move collapsed, his exemplary personality behind the scenes - and the key to unlocking his best form

If last week had gone ever so slightly differently, Cody Gakpo would be spending today in recovery mode after a trip to Porto, preparing for his first Manchester derby.

The Liverpool and Netherlands winger was close to becoming just the sixth man since the turn of the century to swap Merseyside red for Manchester blue, or vice versa.

With a few days left of the transfer window, it was thought Liverpool were happy to pocket a healthy sum for Gakpo – north of £80million – and reinvest it on another winger, such as Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Crystal Palace’s Ismaila Sarr.

Enzo Maresca wanted a wide man that could also play as a back-up No 9 and Gakpo fit the bill perfectly. He was preferred ahead of Iliman Ndiaye, whom City signed instead when Liverpool pulled the plug on Gakpo’s departure.

Modern football fans celebrate transfers as much as goals, so the thrill at a new boy potentially arriving generated a buzz among some Liverpool supporters who did not seem overly fussed about Gakpo’s prospective exit.

After all, last season was a disappointing one for the 27-year-old. He managed seven league goals, only three fewer than in the previous campaign, but beyond the numbers, his performance levels dropped. Like many team-mates, he was inconsistent.

Cody Gakpo has started the season in brilliant form, a major step up from the inconsistency he showed in 2025-26

Had things gone a little differently in the last few days of the transfer window, Gakpo might have been making his Man City debut last night

Gakpo and his representatives had decided to join City, turning down advanced interest from Tottenham. A few signatures on a dotted line were all that was needed to complete the move in his eyes, though Liverpool ultimately blocked it.

The questions their recruitment team pondered in the final days of the market were these: would Minteh or Sarr really be an upgrade on Gakpo? Is it time to give up on a player that signed a five-year deal in August 2025? Will he perform better under the new manager?

Let’s answer those in turn. Minteh, 22, has a high ceiling and may develop into a better player than Gakpo but is injured and there are no guarantees he will fulfil his potential. Sarr is 28 and the way he kicked up a fuss at Crystal Palace to force a move was a red flag.

Selling Gakpo now, when both parties committed their future to each other just 12 months ago, always seemed a strange move and evidence of a lack of joined-up thinking. Signing three wingers in one window (after Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz) would also have represented a huge turnover.

New boss Andoni Iraola is thought to be a huge fan of Gakpo, for his work off the ball as well as on it, with the Dutchman a key component of the relentless and intense pressing patterns Iraola demands of his team.

With Hugo Ekitike a long-term absentee through injury, Gakpo’s versatility is key. He can play down the middle, off both flanks and even in midfield.

Iraola and Gakpo held discussions about his situation every day during the window and were both very honest and open. Iraola liked how the player still put in 100 per cent every day in training sessions, despite the speculation about his future. Other players may not have done the same in that situation.

Gakpo never kicks up a fuss, trains well and is regarded by many as a key member of the dressing room. Many modern footballers have egos bigger than their price-tags but Gakpo is a rounded individual and a likeable personality.

Gakpo provided two assists in Liverpool's impressive 2-0 win at Ipswich. No Premier League player has more than his four goal contributions this term

He never kicks up a fuss, trains well and is regarded by many of his team-mates as a key member of the dressing room

In an interview with Daily Mail Sport in Singapore a few years back, Gakpo discussed how he spent the flight listening to gospel music. He tries to learn a different Bible verse each week and has travelled to Togo, his father’s homeland, for charity projects.

‘Cody is a very smart player,’ said the boss last Friday. ‘He’s in a good place, physically and mentally. I am very happy to keep Cody because he is a very valuable player.’

Captain Virgil van Dijk also pleaded with his compatriot to stay and – along with many others – has rallied around Gakpo after a traumatic summer off the pitch. The 27-year-old and his partner, Noa, lost their son during pregnancy. They named him Elijah.

Gakpo remained in the United States during this heartbreaking period and scored three goals in the World Cup, starting every game as the Netherlands were dumped out in the round of 32 against Morocco in a penalty shootout.

He has carried that form into the new club season, with a goal against Newcastle, an assist against Nottingham Forest and two more against Ipswich. That's the joint-most goal contributions of any player in the Premier League.

His two assists last Friday and his link-up with Alexander Isak, Munoz and Florian Wirtz almost made you forget that £123million marquee signing Bradley Barcola was sitting on the bench. Gakpo and Co were so good that it did not feel outrageous to question how Barcola gets in the side, at least to begin with.

The Frenchman will break into the XI in due course, and might do so tonight against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League after Gakpo was left out of training yesterday as a precaution, but Liverpool now have an attack that can beat anyone, also featuring wonderkid Rio Ngumoha and with Ekitike to return.

Gakpo might not be as flashy as big-money additions Isak and Barcola – but he is still an extremely handy player that has been loved by Jurgen Klopp, Arne Slot and now Iraola.

Gakpo endured a traumatic summer, losing his unborn son Elijah while he was at the World Cup

He has been adored by all three of his managers at Liverpool and looks back to his best despite the speculation around his future

His best days came at the start of his Liverpool career and then in the title-winning campaign of 2024-25, when he had Luis Diaz breathing down his neck. The competition was healthy: the two shared minutes and played with a point to prove.

With Barcola, Munoz and Ngumoha now doing the same, we could see Gakpo return to his best.

Before he joined Liverpool in a £44million deal in January 2023, Gakpo left his future to chance. Ahead of a game for PSV Eindhoven, he spoke to a pastor who told him he would ultimately join Liverpool after Manchester United had pulled out of a deal to sign him in summer 2022.

So Gakpo, in his prayers, said that if he scored one goal in the game, he would join Southampton; two, he would join Leeds; any other number he would stay until January. Both clubs were going all out for him at the time after United had opted to sign Antony instead.

The flying Dutchman scored a hat-trick and ended up staying. Six months later, on the back of a fine World Cup that December in Qatar, he joined Liverpool.

Despite a flirtation with City, he is still there. Maresca's loss is Iraola’s gain.

Sports.title: LIV Golf files for bankruptcy after Saudi backers pulled funding as PGA defectors eye road back to Tour
Sports.content:
LIV GOLF has filed for bankruptcy in a move that will allow leading names such as Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton to walk away before the expiration of their contracts.

A 'Chapter 11' petition was lodged in New Jersey on Tuesday, with the breakaway league locked in a battle to survive ever since their Saudi Arabian backers announced in April that they were pulling the plug.

The latest development had been widely expected, but nonetheless marks a significant milestone in LIV's dramatic fall four years after its arrival triggered an ugly civil war in the sport.

While bankruptcy might allow the circuit to realise its stated ambition of a LIV 2.0, it remains to be seen if their forthcoming union with BC Partners, a private equity group, will be sufficient for the league to extend into a 2027 season.

The greatest unknown at this stage is which of their marquee players will stay with the project in a vastly diminished and less lucrative form, as it is understood that bankruptcy will allow the golfers to exit their contracts, even if they have time still to run.

Bryson DeChambeau's deal expired at the end of the 2026 season but he is expected to recommit in return for equity in the league. The picture around Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton is far more concerning to LIV insiders - both men are contracted through 2028 and Daily Mail Sport sources had indicated prior to bankruptcy that both men were likely to leave in the event of the petition being filed.

Yasir Al Rumayyan (Governor of PIF, Chairman of Aramco) congratulates winning player, Elvis Smylie (Ripper GC) on day 4 of LIV Golf in Riyadh LIV Golf Riyad back in February

Sergio Garcia plays his shot from the 12th tee box during day one of the LIV Invitational

Rahm, for one, hinted at the possibility earlier on Tuesday, when asked at the DP World Tour's Irish Open if he would like to see a pathway back to the PGA Tour. He said: 'I still have a contract with LIV 1.0 that I am more than willing to fulfil, so like I said time will tell.'

The choice of phrase - 'LIV 1.0' – would suggest his loyalty was contingent on his existing terms being honoured in order to continue with LIV.

Having joined the league for a reported $300million in 2023, Rahm is still believed to be owed a nine-figure chunk of that fee, which was structured in instalments across a five-year contract. Along with DeChambeau and Dustin Johnson, the Spaniard is one of the company's ⁠top ​three unsecured creditors, according to the ​petition. Each man is owed more than $5 million, though those sums are understood to relate only to obligations from the third quarter of 2026.

Johnson, Cameron Smith, Adrian Meronk, Hatton and Bubba Watson are also among a group of nine players claiming unpaid fees.

In the likelihood that some now choose to exit, Hatton and Rahm have a ready-made home on the DP World Tour, where they have retained membership during the civil war, but a return to the PGA Tour would require serving a 12-month suspension from their last LIV start. That was the route favoured by Patrick Reed earlier this year when he walked away from an entity that drained the Saudis of more than $5billion since 2022.

Daily Mail Sport previously revealed in May that part of LIV's hope for survival was dependent on players accepting equity in the league instead of the vast sums of cash that fuelled its conception. Such an assumption of interest will now be tested.

CEO of LIV Golf Scott O'Neil: ''Now it is time to enter the next phase of LIV Golf'

Phil Mickelson of HyFlyers GC reacts to his missed putt on the 16th green during Day Two of LIV Michigan at The Cardinal at Saint John's on August 23, 2025 in Plymouth, Michigan

In a letter to LIV fans on Tuesday, the circuit's CEO Scott O'Neil wrote: 'Now it is time to enter the next phase of LIV Golf. Today, we took an important step forward to get there. LIV Golf has entered a court-supervised restructuring process that provides us with the time and framework to address previous financial obligations and complete a transaction that will make the League's next phase a reality. Put simply, this process is designed to build a stronger and more sustainable future for LIV Golf.

'Plenty of well-known companies have taken this path before us, including Marvel Entertainment, Delta Airlines, and Caesars Entertainment, along with sports franchises like the Los Angeles Dodgers, Pittsburgh Penguins, and Leeds United F.C.

'We are entering this process with a clear plan and the support of BC Partners, well-capitalized investors with deep experience in sports and entertainment.

'Our objective is not simply to preserve what we have. It is to make it better.

'The next phase of LIV Golf will be built around a sustainable business model and deeper alignment between players and the League, with team golf at its core. Players will have the opportunity to share directly in the value they help create, while teams will be positioned to grow into enduring global sports businesses. And fans will remain at the centre of everything we do.'

Under O'Neil's plans, a 2027 season would see 10 tournaments, down from the 14 initially scheduled for 2026, and prize funds reduced from around $30m to a figure understood to be between $7m and $10m.

Sports.title: The summer signing giving Unai Emery an extra attacking dimension - and the new man he will be alarmed by: Club Brugge 2-3 Aston Villa
Sports.content:
The summer signing giving Unai Emery an extra attacking dimension - and the new man he will be alarmed by: Club Brugge 2-3 Aston Villa

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A first win of the season, a first goal for Nicolas Jackson and the ideal start to Aston Villa's Champions League campaign – but we may not see the best of Unai Emery's men until after the international break at least.

Heading into this game, Villa had not scored since Brian Madjo's strike in the Super Cup defeat by Paris Saint-Germain nearly a month ago.

But they put that right here as John McGinn, Emi Buendia and Jackson all struck before half-time. Hugo Vetlessen equalised briefly for Club Brugge, who closed the gap in the second half thanks to Nicolo' Tresoldi's penalty.

Both sides missed chances in a chaotic match that would have made Emery desperately nervous. The Villa boss craves control and here Villa rarely had it.

Yet after losing six key players over the summer and making an unconvincing start to the Premier League, this may be the result Villa needed to get their season moving...

Suzuki finding top speed

First Emi Martinez, now Zion Suzuki. Aston Villa certainly love a goalkeeper with 'main character' energy and just like Martinez, Suzuki looks like he will draw the spotlight.

Aston Villa got their first win of the season, a first goal for Nicolas Jackson and the ideal start to the Champions League

Zion Suzuki's range of passing with either foot is remarkable and gives Villa an extra attacking dimension

Where Martinez made his name through his astounding saves and unsavoury antics, it is the kicking that sets Suzuki apart. The Japanese's range of passing with either foot is remarkable and gives Villa an extra attacking dimension.

The game was barely a minute old when Suzuki picked out Aaron Wan-Bissaka, who was on the right touchline halfway inside the Brugge half. Wan-Bissaka and McGinn combined to set up a chance for Buendia but the Argentine missed the target.

Suzuki's kicking will naturally push the opposition back, just as a batter will hit over the top in cricket in order to spread the field. It is great to watch.

There may be some teething problems at the other end, though, as Suzuki's shot-stopping and aerial ability is not quite as convincing. But the early signs are that the £30million have been spent well.

Defensive fragility

Pau Torres was the only member of last season's first choice back four who played here and Villa looked vulnerable, especially out wide.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS Aston Villa (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 7.5; Wan-Bissaka 4.5 (Bogarde 68, 6), Lindelof 7, *TORRES 8*, Maatsen 5.5; J Gomes 6.5, Kamara 7.5 (Barkley 68, 6); McGinn 7, Buendia 7 (Alysson 68, 6), Hemmings 7; Jackson 6.5 (Abraham 81) Scorers: McGinn 11, Buendia 22, Jackson 44 Booked: Maatsen, McGinn, Gomes Manager: Unai Emery 6 Referee: Sandro Schaerer 6

Ezri Konsa, Matty Cash and Lucas Digne were ultra-reliable as Villa finished fourth and won the Europa League – but now Konsa is at Arsenal, Digne is at Paris Saint-Germain and Cash was left at home due to muscle discomfort.

Aaron Wan-Bissaka had a torrid time against Brugge's Spanish winger Jan Virgili and was brought off after 68 minutes. When Konsa was at Villa, he would slot in at right-back at times like these. Instead, Emery had to send on Lamare Bogarde – his fourth-choice central midfielder – to handle Virgili.

It usually takes time for new signings to find their rhythm under Emery. Morgan Rogers was the exception, but players like Digne, Youri Tielemans – now with Manchester United – and Buendia all had to work hard to earn his trust.

Still, Emery will have been a little alarmed by Wan-Bissaka's display. The former Manchester United man, on loan from West Ham, can expect plenty of time in the analysis room after this showing.

Unai Emery will have been a little alarmed by new signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka's display

Emi Buendia is living proof that no player is ever totally out of the picture under Emery at Villa

Never give up

Emi Buendia is living proof that no player is ever totally out of the picture under Emery at Villa.

The playmaker suffered a serious knee injury on the eve of the 2023-24 season and in the following campaign, he was loaned to Bayer Leverkusen in January.

In summer 2025, Buendia was so far out of the picture that he was even considered by Birmingham, who had just been promoted from League One.

But Buendia stayed, won back his place in the team and in May, he scored one of the goals of the season in the Europa League Final to help Villa lift their first major trophy since 1996.

He finished off an excellent move here to restore Villa's lead in the first half. The club have added significant attacking talent this summer, with Johan Manzambi and Ibrahim Mbaye arriving for more than £100million combined and Alejandro Garnacho joining on loan. All of them will have a tough job to squeeze Buendia out of the team.

Sports.title: Konstantinos Karetsas health latest as Borussia Dortmund chief speaks out on winger
Sports.content:
Konstantinos Karetsas health latest as Borussia Dortmund chief speaks out on winger

Borussia Dortmund issued an update on Konstantinos Karetsas at half-time of their Champions League match against Villarreal - and club officials have now spoken

View 2 Images Konstantinos Karetsas covered his face while lying supine on the pitch (Image: Borussia Dortmund via Getty Images)

Borussia Dortmund sporting director Nils-Ole Book says Konstantinos Karetsas was unable to speak after being stretchered off the pitch during their Champions League match against Villarreal. The summer signing from Genk signalled to the sideline that he could not continue midway through the first half, sitting down on the pitch and covering his face with both hands before lying supine.

‌



Karetsas, 18, was making his Champions League debut. The crowd applauded him as he was carried off on a stretcher.

‌



Dortmund described the issue as 'circulatory problems'. The club confirmed that he was going to the hospital for further examinations.

‌



Seven players could miss Napoli vs Arsenal through injury as surgery confirmed in statement READ MORE :

A statement shared on X at half-time of the match reads: "Konstantinos Karetsas had to leave the field due to circulatory problems. Kosta is doing well under the circumstances and is on his way to the hospital for further tests."

The former Dortmund captain, Mats Hummels, was working as a pundit at Westfalenstadion. He said of Karetsas on Amazon Prime Video: "When the doctors didn't even look at the legs, but only at the upper body, it sent shivers down my spine.

"We don't wish such a story on anyone. These are really nasty pictures that we had to see."

‌



View 2 Images Konstantinos Karetsas was carried off the pitch on a stretcher (Image: Alex Gottschalk/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images)

The club's sporting director Book then said of Karetsas on Sky after the match: "He was substituted due to circulatory problems. It came very suddenly, he sat down and was taken to the hospital for further examinations, where he is now.

"And of course we'll wait and see. Of course, that clouds the mood significantly."

‌



He continued: "I went out with him, but he wasn't able to speak directly at that moment. Of course, we hope that it will get better very, very quickly and that it's nothing serious. But now, especially after the game, we don't have any new information yet."

‌



"At first, I assumed that he might have some muscular problems. But then he didn't touch his thigh at all and was even carried down on a stretcher."

Ricken explained that the reasons Karetsas was having tests is "to rule out everything in the end." The former player continued: "We have to wait and see what the next few days will bring."

Sports.title: LIV Golf files for bankruptcy protection as star players owed £33m free to leave
Sports.content:
LIV Golf files for bankruptcy protection as star players owed £33m free to leave

The future of LIV Golf has been plunged into further doubt after it filed for bankruptcy protection, with star players such as Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau and Dustin Johnson owed a combined £33million

View 2 Images LIV Golf is facing financial trouble (Image: Brian Spurlock/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

The downfall of LIV Golf has continued after the controversial breakaway league filed for bankruptcy protection. LIV executives are seeking protection for at least $45million (£33m) owed to players, who'll have the option to leave as a result of the move.

‌



On Tuesday, a Chapter 11 petition was filed in the United States. LIV says that the decision was made to 'preserve the company's business' after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) made the decision to withdraw its multibillion-dollar funding in April.

‌



A new investor, BC Partners, has since been found but LIV's financial problems remain. Topping the list of the series' largest 30 creditors - as outlined by documents in the petition - is two-time major winner Jon Rahm, who has the largest unsecured claim of $7.5m (£5.5m).

‌



The Spaniard is joined by Bryson DeChambeau ($5.7m - £4.2m), Dustin Johnson ($5.5m - £4.1m), Cameron Smith ($4.8m - £3.5m) and Tyrrell Hatton ($3.4m - £2.5m). Brooks Koepka has an unsecured claim of $1.7m (£1.25m), despite rejoining the PGA Tour in January.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Tiger Woods avoids jail with last-minute plea deal over reckless driving charge that ended in horror crash READ MORE :

LIV has plans to continue - dependant on players' involvement - but announced last month that it was 'scaling back operations'. The majority of its employees were laid off at the beginning of September.

‌



Ahead of this week's Irish Open, Rahm was asked if he knows what the future holds for LIV. "Yes and no, it hasn't really changed from my last interview in Indianapolis a few weeks ago," he told BBC Sport.

"And there's just a lot of things in place, right? There's a lot of things that could happen and it's one of those things where time's gonna tell."

Rahm went on to say: "To be fair for us people that joined LIV, I'm pretty good at dealing with turbulence ... I still have a contract with LIV 1.0 that I'm more than willing to fulfil, so like I said, time will tell."

‌



Should players quit LIV Golf? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Jon Rahm was tight-lipped when asked about LIV Golf's future (Image: Richard Heathcote/Getty Images)

The 31-year-old reportedly has more than $100m (£74m) left on his multi-year contract with LIV which he signed at the end of 2023. Talks will now be held with star players such as Rahm to determine the series' place on the golfing circuit.

‌



Founded in 2021 to a wave of backlash from the golfing world, LIV pledged to create 'an ownership structure aligning players' interests with the league's long-term success'. But now its future is in major jeopardy.

LIV chief executive Scott O'Neil, however, commented on Tuesday: "The people of LIV Golf, led by the players, have continued to show incredible resilience, commitment, and a shared belief in what we are building.

"Thanks to their tireless work, LIV Golf has created a foundation to entertain and inspire the next generation of global golf fans around the world."

Sports.content:
Seven players could miss Napoli vs Arsenal through injury as surgery confirmed in statement

Arsenal and Napoli are both missing multiple players for their first match in the league phase of this season's Champions League, as injuries are already biting

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal are dealing with multiple injury issues in defence ahead of ther clash with Napoli (Image: James Fearn, Getty Images)

Several players may miss Arsenal's Champions League match against Napoli due to injury. The Gunners continue to deal with multiple absences in their squad, while the Serie A side also have a similar number of setbacks to contend with.

‌



Mikel Arteta was sent off the last time Arsenal played a Champions League match in Naples, with Gonzalo Higuain and Jose Callejon firing Rafael Benítez's team to a 2-0 win in December 2013. However, they have won in Campania since.

‌



Unai Emery guided them to a 1-0 win during the Europa League semi-finals in 2019. Arteta will hope to right the wrongs of nearly 13 years ago tonight.

‌



Arsenal escape UEFA fine after being forced to cancel Champions League press conference READ MORE :

Scott McTominay health update as Napoli issue statement following heart surgery READ MORE :

However, the Gunners remain without William Saliba. He is still recovering from a back injury sustained while on international duty with France during the summer's World Cup.

Cristhian Mosquera has, meanwhile, been nursing a muscle problem over the past week, which forced the centre-back to sit out Arsenal's Premier League victory over Chelsea at the weekend. Arteta, however, hinted that the decision to leave Mosquera out of the matchday squad at Emirates Stadium was largely precautionary.

Arteta said: "He had a muscular issue. We think it is not too much, but we need to wait and see in the next few days how it evolves."

‌



View 2 Images Defender Jurrien Timber is training with his Arsenal team-mates again (Image: David Price, Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Jurrien Timber is yet to pull on an Arsenal shirt this season following minor surgery during the summer. However, he has been putting in the hard yards on the training pitch ahead of this week's fixture.

Arteta offered an encouraging update on Timber's fitness last week when quizzed about the Netherlands international's rehabilitation. The Arsenal boss said: "He's in really good condition at the moment, he's been a few weeks on the pitch and has been training with us, so he's in a really good place."

‌



Napoli will also be missing several key figures when they host Arsenal. Scott McTominay, notably, is ruled out.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: 'New signing' dubbed 'dangerous' as Red Devils land record-breaking deal
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: 'New signing' dubbed 'dangerous' as Red Devils land record-breaking deal

Round-up as Manchester United prepare for their return to the Champions League

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has overseen a mixed start to the season for Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United are looking for lift-off following a frustratingly mixed start to the season. Head coach Michael Carrick is looking to build on the momentum gained from guiding United to third place and back the Champions League.

‌



But despite a kind-looking start on paper, the Red Devils have just four points from three games and sit 11th in the Premier League table. On Sunday, Carrick's side were pegged back by Everton deep into added time as they were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw.

‌



United are now preparing to return to the Champions League and their first appearance in the competition's new format, which sees an initial 36-team league phase.

‌



United kick off their campaign against the Azerbaijani side Sabah at Old Trafford on Thursday, before attention returns to domestic duty and Sunday's Manchester derby. Here's a round-up of the latest news from Old Trafford…

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Rashford 'smelling of roses'

Peter Schmeichel said Marcus Rashford is like a new signing as he hailed the returning winger's early-season form. After loan spells at Aston Villa and Barcelona, Rashford has looked something close to his brilliant best since being reintegrated into the team after a summer transfer failed to materialise.

‌



Manchester United reach new agreement as cash injection confirmed READ MORE :

United legend Schmeichel was especially impressed with the forward at Everton. He told Viaplay: "Coming away from that game, Rashford is now smelling of roses. I thought he was absolutely fantastic."

The Dane added: "It just shows that there's some intent now for Marcus to go back to what he was for Manchester United four years ago, when he scored 30 goals in one season.

"He was playing like this. Seeing his team-mates, putting them in, getting the ball into good positions, stepping up, getting the ball into the box. He wasn't trying to do everything himself, [he was] trying to be dangerous.

‌



"If that's what we get for this season, welcome back, Marcus. We have missed you, because he is then one of the top players in the world."

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford looks to have a new lease of life (Image: Peter Byrne/PA Wire)

Record deal signed

United have landed a record sleeve sponsorship deal with a financial technology company. The lucrative tie-up will see SumUp - described by the club as a "leading global fintech company" - feature on United's first-team shirts, replacing DXC Technology.

‌



It is the club's biggest ever sleeve sponsorship deal, although it is unclear exactly how much the contract will be worth. It is believed to be worth more than the recently agreed training kit sponsorship deal with Betway, which will reportedly net the club around £20million per year.

United's chief business officer, Marc Armstrong, said: "The new agreement supports our commercial growth strategy and reflects the continued appeal of Manchester United as a platform for ambitious brands looking to connect with audiences around the world."

SumUp branding will appear on the shirts for the first time against Sabah. It will also appear on the academy and women's teams' shirts.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Julian Alvarez behaviour speaks volumes as private chat with team-mate emerges
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Julian Alvarez behaviour speaks volumes as private chat with team-mate emerges

A look at the latest headlines surrounding Arsenal as they get set to return to the Champions League on Wednesday night with a trip to Napoli

View 3 Images Julian Alvarez's behaviour at Atletico Madrid has emerged (Image: Cesar Ortiz Gonzalez/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Julian Alvarez's behaviour following a failed move to Arsenal has been revealed, with Lautaro Martinez offering insight into the striker's mindset. The Gunners were pushing for the Argentina international towards the end of the window but he ultimately remained with Atletico Madrid.

‌



With that, Mikel Arteta will rely upon Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres as forward options for the season. This has ultimately been working well, as the Gunners have won all three Premier League games of the 2026/27 campaign.

‌



Now a tricky opening clash away at Napoli is coming up in the Champions League. Arteta's side have travelled to Italy for the fixture as they aim to reach the final once again.

‌



Here, Mirror Football has the latest coming out of the red side of north London.

David Raya reveals what now sets Arsenal apart from Premier League title rivals READ MORE :

Arsenal sent Champions League warning as two teams who can stop them named READ MORE :

Alvarez behaviour emerges

Alvarez is said to be back to "new" following his failed transfer saga this summer. The Argentine striker was desperate for a move to Barcelona, with Arsenal also circling, but neither move materialised.

The 26-year-old missed three training sessions in a row, citing illness, and did not travel with the team to face Sevilla. He returned in a 3-0 loss to Athletic Club earlier in September and impressed, despite continued jeers from the Atleti fans.

‌



This effort is now said to have translated in training with AS claiming he is "a new Julian Alvarez." The Spanish news outlet stated that the striker took part in an intense session which focused on pressure, ball circulation and 'stealing.'

View 3 Images Alvarez is reportedly a 'new' man and has got his head down (Image: Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images)

Alvarez reportedly scored during this training session and also put in extra work with a physical trainer to build up his fitness as others stretched. Atleti manager Diego Simeone discussed the striker before last weekend's game, stating that he hopes the failed transfer was "a learning experience."

Simeone said: "Julian Alvarez will be in the squad tomorrow. He's training well, and we expect the best from him, just as we do from all his team-mates. For me, life is full of opportunities, and Julian now has an opportunity. A lot of the time, we spend our lives judging.

"We need to worry less about that and learn more. I hope this has served as a learning experience for him. I hope he's happy and, as [Paulo] Futre [Atletico Madrid's director of football] told him yesterday in a lovely video... that he shows it by scoring goals."

‌



Team-mate speaks out

View 3 Images Lautaro Martinez has spoken out about international team-mate and friend Alvarez (Image: Pablo Morano/BSR Agency/Getty Images)

Martinez has spoken out about Arsenal target Alvarez, showing support for the 26-year-old following his transfer saga. The fellow Argentina international has travelled to Madrid with Inter Milan to face Real and explained Alvarez's situation from his perspective.

The 29-year-old said: "I spoke with him, sent him a message, and showed him my support. Beyond the fact that we share the same position and competed for a spot on the national team, he’s a friend.

"The situation he’s going through and is going through isn’t easy, but the decision is his clubs."

Hailing Alvarez's talent, Martinez added: "I wish him all the best and hope he gets well soon and continues to show what he has shown so far, that he is one of the best players in the world."

Sports.title: Lionel Messi splashes out on second football club as 'full takeover agreement reached'
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi splashes out on second football club as 'full takeover agreement reached'

Lionel Messi could become the owner of another football club with a deal reportedly on the verge of being announced

View 2 Images Lionel Messi could be about to complete a full takeover of another club (Image: Megan Briggs/Getty Images)

Lionel Messi has reportedly agreed to complete a full takeover of a Spanish second division club, just over a week after announcing his retirement from international football. Messi, 39, is currently in the middle of his fourth season in Major League Soccer with Inter Miami, and already appears to have an eye on the future.

‌



The Barcelona legend helped Argentina reach the final of the World Cup in the summer, before his country suffered a 1-0 defeat to Spain in the showpiece match in New Jersey.

‌



Messi signed a new contract with Miami earlier this year that will run until the end of the 2028 MLS season, at which point the former Paris Saint-Germain will be 41 years old.

‌



A fresh report from Spain, meanwhile, has claimed that Messi is now venturing further into the world of club ownership, with a deal appearing to be close to completion to oversee a full takeover.

Diego Simeone makes honest Julian Alvarez admission ahead of Liverpool clash READ MORE :

Spanish publication AS has claimed that Messi is on the verge of acquiring a 100 per cent stake in La Liga 2 club CD Eldense, who are currently sat in the relegation zone.

It has been reported that an agreement has been reached for Messi to become the majority owner of the Spanish second-tier club, with his lawyers said to be holding talks with TH, a Colombian investment group.

‌



The report goes on to claim that an official announcement confirming the full takeover from Messi could happen within the next few days.

Should a deal get over the line, it would be the second club under Messi’s ownership, with the other being Cornella, which plays in the fifth tier of Spanish football.

It was just last month that Messi announced his retirement from international football, with his final match for Argentina being the defeat to Spain in the World Cup final in July.

‌

Messi announced his retirement just a few weeks after his father, Jorge, passed away, and posted an emotional message confirming his plan to no longer represent his country.

"After all this time that has passed since the final, and after much thought, I want to announce to everyone that I am retiring from the National Team,” Messi posted on Instagram.”It was a decision that hurt, and still hurts, to my core, but I understand that it's the right time.

‌



"I swear that I always gave my all, not just in the last few years when we won everything, but before that too. I always fought and gave everything for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you proud to be Argentinian through football.

"There's not much time left, and chapters are closing, and this is one that hurts me deeply. I love, loved, and will always love being on the National Team. I've given everything I have; I have nothing more to give, and besides, there are some great young players coming up behind me who deserve to be there.

View 2 Images Lionel Messi announced his retirement from international football last month (Image: Leonardo Fernandez/Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"Thank you for all the love and support over these 20 years. I'm going to miss hearing you all from the inside so much. Now I'm going to be just one of you, cheering and supporting you from the sidelines (in good times and bad, even more so).

"Thank you to my family for always being there, for accompanying me on this beautiful but difficult journey. Thank you to each and every one of the coaches, teammates, and managers I had the privilege of working with. I take with me unforgettable memories and moments.”

‌



Messi continued: "I leave with the peace and pride of having given you, along with my teammates, dreamlike moments. It was incredible to have experienced it with you all. I love you!

"Thank you, God, for making me Argentinian. Go Argentina! I wrote these words on July 21st, two days after the final. Today, after what happened to my dad, I'm even more convinced than before."
