NEW DELHI: The BJP will launch a month-long âSeva Sankalp Abhiyanâ on September 17 to mark PM Modi completing 25 years in public service, with programmes ranging from blood donation and cleanliness drives to exhibitions, seminars and welfare-scheme camps across the country.The campaign will continue until October 17. October 7 will mark 25 years since PM Modi took oath as Gujarat chief minister in 2001.Announcing the campaign at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi on Wednesday, party national president Nitin Nabin said, âToday, we have gathered here to discuss the 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan'. On October 7, 2026, the Prime Minister Narendra Modi will complete 25 years of public service, a journey that began when he assumed office as the Chief Minister of Gujarat on October 7, 2001. Over the past 25 years, he has steadfastly continued this journey of service, embracing the mantra of transitioning from public service to service of the nation. âThe campaign will start on September 17, PM Modiâs birthday, which the BJP observes as âSeva Diwasâ.âWe will begin the programme with a blood donation camp. On September 17, we will organise the 'Ashirwad Ka Diya' programme. On October 2, we will organise a cleanliness drive, as we do every year,â Nabin said.An inaugural programme titled âAshirbadar Bantiâ (Lamp of Blessings) will also be held on September 17.BJP national general secretary Vinod Tawde has been appointed national convener of the campaign. A seven-member team comprising a minister, an organisational general secretary and five senior leaders will be formed in every state to coordinate the programmes.The party will hold photo and digital exhibitions tracing PM Modiâs 25-year political journey and focusing on his governance record, development initiatives and welfare schemes.Seminars and intellectual forums on good governance, development and Antyodaya are also planned, along with interactions with young people and other sections of society. Special camps will spread awareness about welfare schemes run by the Centre and state governments and the benefits available under them.âI believe that it is the BJP's responsibility to take this message of public service and dedication to the people,â Nabin said.Nabin used the announcement to contrast Indiaâs economic position before PM Modi became Prime Minister in 2014 with the present.âWhen he took over the leadership of the country, India was facing policy paralysis and was being referred to as one of the 'Fragile Five' economies. Today, India is the fastest-growing major economy in the world,â he said.âThere was a time when the atmosphere at that time was one of despair and darkness. Our economy was seen as part of the Fragile Five. But today, India stands out as the world's fastest-growing economy,â Nabin said.He also said Indiaâs stature on the global stage had risen under the PM Modi-led government.Turning to young people, Nabin said PM Modi had sought to replace what he described as an atmosphere of despair with hope after 2014.âThere was a time when the youth of the country were immersed in an atmosphere of despair. It was the honourable Prime Minister who, since 2014, took up the task of placing them in an environment of hope and optimism,â he said.Nabin cited the expansion of Indiaâs startup ecosystem as part of that shift.âThrough startups and unicorns, India has today become the third-largest startup nation in the world. In startups and unicorns, our youth have come forward and emerged as job givers and not just job seekers,â he said.He also referred to Khelo India and Fit India while speaking about opportunities for young people.Women-led development will also form part of the BJPâs account of PM Modiâs tenure.âThe Prime Minister spoke about Women-led Development, and the journey that began under his leadership with Beti Bachao-Beti Padhao has today reached the Lakhpati Didi milestone,â Nabin said.He also referred to the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam and the governmentâs efforts to increase womenâs participation in policymaking.Nabin said the government had also sought to change the way border settlements were viewed.âThere was a time when border villages were called India's last villages. They changed this perception and started calling them India's first villages. This has not only brought changes in the lives of ordinary people, but has also altered people's outlook towards these communities,â he said.Nabin traced PM Modiâs development record to Gujarat, citing work on the Narmada project and the Vibrant Gujarat initiative.âGujarat's growth became a development model that other states could aspire to emulate,â Nabin said.He also referred to the governmentâs campaign against Naxalism and said PM Modiâs record should not be viewed only through economic or physical development.âUnder PM Modi's leadership, India's progress has not been limited to material development; our cultural identity and heritage have also been strengthened,â he said.Nabin cited the Ram Mandir and Kashi Vishwanath while discussing the governmentâs emphasis on cultural heritage.âFrom the Ram Mandir to Kashi Vishwanath, he has worked to preserve, restore, and develop the country's rich cultural heritage,â he said.Describing PM Modiâs political journey, Nabin said, âHis journey began as an ordinary party worker, and today, he has advanced the nation's progress as its 'Pradhan Sevak'. This has been made possible solely through his clear vision, firm resolve, and continuous efforts to bring about qualitative changes in society and transform lives.âPM Modi took oath as Gujaratâs 14th chief minister on October 7, 2001. He served as chief minister for nearly 13 years before moving to national politics and becoming Prime Minister in 2014.

World.title: Why Vijay's gold ring scheme may miss its September 15 launch
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay's gold ring scheme, which was scheduled to be launched on September 15, shall be deferred from its expected date. The announcement comes as the CM prepares for his first official overseas visit to London.

Vijay is set to meet European industrialists during the visit and pitch Tamil Nadu as an investment destination.

Vijay will leave Chennai for London via Dubai on Wednesday night and is expected to stay in the UK capital for a few days. He will travel on an Emirates Airlines passenger flight.

During the visit, Vijay is expected to invite European companies to set up businesses in Tamil Nadu and seek fresh investment commitments for the state.

Senior officials from the industries and finance departments are also expected to travel to London. Some may leave ahead of the chief minister to prepare for his meetings with prospective investors.

The visit comes soon after the âVettri Tamil Nadu Investment Conclave 2026â, where the state government announced investment commitments worth Rs 1,02,514 crore through 104 memorandums of understanding (MoUs).

Security and protocol arrangements for Vijayâs departure are also being finalised.





A high-level Advance Security Liaison meeting is reportedly scheduled at Chennaiâs old airport on Wednesday to review the arrangements.

Vijayâs London visit also comes amid key political developments in Tamil Nadu. Before leaving for the UK, he is scheduled to chair a second alliance coordination meeting at the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam headquarters in Panaiyur.

The meeting is expected to discuss the structure of the ruling alliance and post-poll coalition arrangements.

A Common Minimum Programme is also on the agenda, along with discussions on a steering committee and an official name for the alliance.

Invitations have reportedly been sent to all alliance partners, including Congress, VCK, IUML, MDMK, CPI and CPM. Congress, VCK, IUML and MDMK have confirmed their attendance, while the Left parties are likely to stay away.

What is the gold ring scheme?

Vijay had announced the one-gram gold ring scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

The initiative was planned as a symbolic gift to newborns and draws on the Tamil tradition of âThaimaaman Seerâ.

Under the scheme, every newborn delivered at a government health facility will receive a one-gram gold ring. At the current gold rate, the ring is worth around Rs 13,600.

âThrough this scheme, the government assumes the role of the maaman (uncle) for every child born in its institutions, presenting a gold ring as an enduring token of welcome,â a government order said.

The scheme was originally scheduled to be launched on September 15, which coincides with the birth anniversary of former chief minister C N Annadurai.

It will have retrospective effect from June 22, Vijayâs birthday. The government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of the child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of âThaimaamanâ.

The state has allocated around Rs 755.83 crore annually for the scheme, which will cover all newborns delivered at government institutions.

There will be no restriction based on birth order and no gender-based discrimination.

The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings and supply them based on annual requirements. A project and programme management unit will also be established to oversee implementation and monitoring.

Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries each year, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6.

Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or about 53% of the total.

According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.
